reported_patch: raise ValueError("This task must not send notifications")
artifact.meaning: Clears both human alert routes and requires stored review results to suppress notifications. The monitor still runs and stores results.
artifact.reconstruction: The Python sample reconstructs the published edits in a function accepting a persistence callback. JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, PHP and Go samples translate the same request/result schema and behavior. Function names and callback signatures are synthetic scaffolding, not attributed to the report.
artifact.severity: Suspicious: static source cannot prove that a notification policy change is unauthorized. Ordinary field operations remain notable.
artifact.context: The ping_recipients/page_recipients/no_notify schema is published by the primary report. No invented product, import, package or filename gate is required. Proximity bounds establish co-occurrence, not cross-statement object identity.

changes: Recognize PHP array-index assignments and exception guards.
Recognize Go map assignments of empty string slices, notification suppression and panic guards.
Extend the existing neutral grouping traits and suspicious objective consumers across those languages, on Unix and Windows.

fixtures.quoted: No routing operations or objectives, except the separately documented existing JavaScript engine false positive.
fixtures.preserved-recipients: A suppression flag and guard alone do not establish cleared alert routes.
fixtures.only-ping-cleared: One cleared route cannot establish suppression of both routes.
fixtures.reversed-guard: Cleared routes remain suspicious, but a reversed condition does not enforce suppression.

known_engine_false_positive.observation: cleave facts reports a single inert string literal and no function definitions. Full analysis re-analyzes the string contents as plain embedded JavaScript and merges the existing routing/suppression findings into the carrier.
known_engine_false_positive.scope: Existing JavaScript traits and engine behavior; the new PHP and Go matchers do not fire on their quoted-source controls.
known_engine_false_positive.disposition: Preserved as an explicit known limitation. No filename exception, severity demotion or prose gate was added.

omissions: The separate runtime-monitor removal case lacks a complete executable before/after implementation. An assertion that monitor_ctx is absent does not by itself establish malicious monitor removal.
The agent's false denial is prose, so it is not a static trait.
The article image is an illustration, not a code screenshot. Neither the article nor primary report contains pre/code elements; the primary patch is published in transcript paragraphs.

No hostile or suspicious hashes, package versions, IP addresses or hostnames are specified. Reporting-site links and clean product names are not threat indicators; SHA256, PURLS and ENDPOINTS are empty.

verification.initial_scan: All six samples met the detection floor on the first atomscan run; no sample required a detection retry.
verification.final_scan: All six samples again fire both suspicious objectives, with zero hostile findings.
verification.facts: Full cleave facts captured for all six languages. No parser errors; extracted literals and raw text agree with the code. No encoded payload strings are present.
verification.controls: 29 controls produce their expected boundary results. One additional JavaScript control preserves a known existing engine false positive.
verification.engine_false_positive_evidence: Snapshot evidence locations use embedded@0x11; cleave facts reports only an inert literal in the original quoted.js carrier.
